name: Abū Muslim Muʿādh ibn Muslim al-Harrāʾ
summary: Kufan grammarian of the first generation, a teacher of al-Kisāʾī, whom later scholars name as the first to treat taṣrīf as a subject of its own.
bio: Muʿādh ibn Muslim was a client of the Anṣār in Kufa, called al-Harrāʾ because he sold garments of Herat. Al-Zubaydī places him in the first generation of Kufan grammarians with Abū Jaʿfar al-Ruʾāsī, and he taught al-Kisāʾī. He lived very long, by the reports close to a hundred years, and died in 187/803.
Later scholars, al-Suyūṭī among them, name him as the first to lay down taṣrīf, the building of words from their roots, as a field of study; the claim rests on reports, since no book of his survives.
uncertain: The claim that he founded taṣrīf is late, and no work of his has come down to us.

sources.title: al-Zubaydī, Ṭabaqāt al-naḥwiyyīn wa-l-lughawiyyīn, entry 57 (Arabic text, OpenITI)
